facts.text: The EU Machinery Regulation governs machine safety and conformity, the AI Act and its 2026 amendment govern artificial intelligence, the Product Liability Directive governs liability for harm, and the Data Act governs access to machine-generated data for machines sold in Europe from 2027.
facts.quote: These four European Union laws set the legal ground for a machine sold in Europe from 2027

facts.text: The Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 was adopted on 14 June 2023.
facts.quote: The Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, adopted 14 June 2023

facts.text: The Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 applies from 20 January 2027 and replaces the Machinery Directive 2006/42/EC, which covers machines placed on the market until 19 January 2027.
facts.quote: applies from 20 January 2027 and replaces the Machinery Directive 2006/42/EC, which covers machines placed on the market until 19 January 2027

facts.text: The booklet identifies the Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 as the core market-access law for a product arriving in mid-2027.
facts.quote: For a product arriving in mid-2027 it is "the core market-access law".

facts.text: The Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 requires risk reduction, safe and reliable control systems, protection against corruption (cybersecurity), and technical documentation.
facts.quote: It requires risk reduction, safe and reliable control systems, protection against corruption (cybersecurity) and technical documentation

facts.text: The Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 contains no automatic-braking test matrix.
facts.quote: contains no automatic-braking test matrix [Chapter 3]

facts.text: Annex I Part A of the Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 lists safety components with fully or partially self-evolving behaviour using machine learning approaches ensuring safety functions, and machinery embedding those components; both need a notified body.
facts.quote: Annex I Part A lists "safety components with fully or partially self-evolving behaviour using machine learning approaches ensuring safety functions" and machinery embedding them, both needing a notified body.

facts.text: Annex II of the Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 makes software ensuring safety functions a safety component.
facts.quote: Annex II makes "software ensuring safety functions" a safety component.

facts.text: The Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 reportedly requires logging of safety-related decisions and software versions for some machinery.
facts.quote: it reportedly requires logging of safety-related decisions and software versions for some machinery [Chapters 3, 7]

facts.text: Whether a frozen trained model is self-evolving under the Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 is disputed and unsettled.
facts.quote: Whether a frozen trained model is "self-evolving" is disputed and unsettled

facts.text: The harmonized-standards list for the Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 was still being prepared in 2026.
facts.quote: the harmonized-standards list was still being prepared in 2026

facts.text: The booklet found no wording in the Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 accepting simulation as evidence.
facts.quote: no wording accepting simulation as evidence was found [Chapters 3, 12]

facts.text: The AI Act (EU) 2024/1689 is the general law on artificial intelligence.
facts.quote: The AI Act (EU) 2024/1689 is the general law on artificial intelligence.

facts.text: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, called the Digital Omnibus on AI, was adopted on 8 July 2026 and entered into force on 27 July 2026.
facts.quote: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, the "Digital Omnibus on AI", adopted 8 July 2026 and in force 27 July 2026

facts.text: The Digital Omnibus on AI (EU) 2026/1744 rewrote the AI Act timeline and directly amended the Machinery Regulation.
facts.quote: rewrote its timeline and amended the Machinery Regulation directly

facts.text: Under the Digital Omnibus on AI (EU) 2026/1744, high-risk obligations for AI embedded in products apply from 2 August 2028.
facts.quote: high-risk obligations for AI embedded in products now apply from 2 August 2028

facts.text: The Digital Omnibus on AI (EU) 2026/1744 removes machinery from direct AI Act high-risk classification.
facts.quote: machinery is taken out of direct AI Act high-risk classification

facts.text: AI health and safety requirements for machinery are to arrive through delegated acts under the Machinery Regulation by 2 August 2028.
facts.quote: AI health and safety requirements for machinery are to arrive through delegated acts under the Machinery Regulation by the same date

facts.text: The Digital Omnibus on AI (EU) 2026/1744 defines a safety function as one that prevents or mitigates risks to health, safety or property.
facts.quote: a "safety function" is defined as one that prevents or mitigates risks to health, safety or property

facts.text: The delegated acts establishing machinery AI health and safety requirements had not been adopted by 1 October 2026.
facts.quote: Those delegated acts had not been adopted by 1 October 2026

facts.text: The booklet warns against treating machine learning as unregulated until 2028 because general machinery and functional-safety duties exist in 2027.
facts.quote: machine learning cannot be treated as "unregulated until 2028", because the general machinery and functional-safety duties exist in 2027

facts.text: The Product Liability Directive (EU) 2024/2853 applies to products placed on the market after 9 December 2026.
facts.quote: The Product Liability Directive (EU) 2024/2853 applies to products placed on the market after 9 December 2026.

facts.text: Under the Product Liability Directive (EU) 2024/2853, software, including updates, is a product.
facts.quote: Software, including updates, is a product

facts.text: Under the Product Liability Directive (EU) 2024/2853, courts may order disclosure of evidence.
facts.quote: courts may order disclosure of evidence

facts.text: Under the Product Liability Directive (EU) 2024/2853, a defect is presumed if the defendant fails to disclose evidence or technical complexity makes proof excessively difficult.
facts.quote: a defect is presumed if the defendant fails to disclose or where technical complexity makes proof "excessively difficult"

facts.text: The booklet's product-liability review concludes that the assumptions and gaps of a disclosed simulation safety case become the claimant's exhibit.
facts.quote: "the assumptions and gaps of a disclosed simulation safety case become the claimant's exhibit"

facts.text: The EU Data Act gives users rights to data from connected products.
facts.quote: The EU Data Act gives users rights to data from connected products

facts.text: The booklet did not verify the application dates of the EU Data Act or the Cyber Resilience Act.
facts.quote: its application dates, and those of the Cyber Resilience Act, were not verified [Chapter 13]

facts.text: The booklet identifies 9 December 2026 for liability, 20 January 2027 for machinery, and 2 August 2028 for machinery AI requirements as three dates falling inside the program window.
facts.quote: Three dates fall inside the program window: 9 December 2026 (liability), 20 January 2027 (machinery) and 2 August 2028 (AI requirements for machinery)

facts.text: If machine learning performs the braking function, the conservative program plan budgets for a notified body from 2027 and expects machinery-specific AI rules by 2028.
facts.quote: If machine learning performs the braking function, the conservative plan budgets for a notified body from 2027 and expects machinery-specific AI rules by 2028

facts.text: Every simulation assumption in the safety case should be written as if a court will read it.
facts.quote: Every simulation assumption in the safety case should be written as if a court will read it [Chapter 13].
